producer_report.summary: I re-read the mounted firstmate tree and rebuilt the study. It now has 40 claims (it had 22), and the three corrections are in. Teardown reopens the backlog item, rather than closing it, when the item is still an open captain call (c23, c24). With yolo on, firstmate merges green work itself, and with it off the captain approves (c25, c11); a red PR is never merged under either setting without an explicit captain instruction (c26). Only a recorded PR or a cleanup frees a capacity place, and relaunches and secondmates are never counted (c30–c32). Other gaps I found and added: places are counted across all local homes and every clone of one origin but not remote homes (c33); an unreadable task record makes the spawn refuse (c34); counting and publishing share one lock, and freeing a place takes no lock (c35); with no capacity declaration, dispatch stays uncapped (c36); teardown's landed-work test, scout and secondmate rules, lost-slot exit 4, and a PR lookup when none was recorded (c28, c37–c40). All older claims are re-cited at the mounted tree's current line numbers. The model gets a "Held open" state with two transitions into it (t9 teardown, t10 replay of a retention record). Rationales ra5–ra8 are new. Finding f3 is new and the existing findings are updated. The introduction, summaries and glossary are rewritten to match. xtask/src/site.rs needed one edit: its test hardcoded 8 transition summaries and now expects 10. validation.json needed no change: every rule already passes against the tree. `cargo test --locked`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- site` all pass. I could not open the built page (the tool blocks paths outside the working directory), so the pin and the three corrections on the rendered page are checked only through the xtask page tests.

open_issues: The brief's pinned source SHA (fc8972cd...) differs from the SHA recorded in pin.json and in every claim (6407052f...). I followed the reading and left pin.json unchanged. The study test accepts quotes only against the mounted tree. So the claims carry 6407052f and the quotes are verified against the mounted tree. If the mount really is fc8972cd, the mapping is wrong, and the owner should decide whether pin.json should change.
validation.json is unchanged. Its results already pass every rule, and it is a recorded result rather than something I could regenerate.
c27 (the PR-merge and local-merge scripts refuse an unproved merge) rests only on AGENTS.md. I did not read fm-pr-merge.sh or fm-merge-local.sh, and the study says so.
The 'captain-hold answer' step that closes a held-open item was not read, and finding f3 says so.
mistakes: My first draft of c37 cited the wrong line range for 'Work has landed when it is'; the test caught it and I fixed it.
I left a stray duplicate text key in the t4 summary in intro.json; I removed it before running any checks.
I briefly added t10 to the f2 finding (the 'no guard' note); t10 has a real guard, so I reverted that.
learnings: The brief names the pinned source as fc8972cdc16f988a84588ac6f4ce4e3b0abf20b9, while pin.json and every claim use 6407052f4c521e39401ce2305dfa45d201249827.

Before my edits, 18 of 22 claims and rationales ra2 and ra3 failed the study rules test against the mounted tree, because the mounted tree's line numbers differ from the ones the old claims cited (AGENTS.md section 7 is shifted by about 6 lines, bin/fm-spawn.sh capacity code by about 165).
The rules test checks line ranges and quotes only against the mounted tree. A quote must sit inside one source line, so I cited multi-line ranges with short single-line fragments.
xtask/src/site.rs has a test that hardcodes the number of transition summaries, so adding transitions to the model means updating it.
